Subject: FastCart follow-up: throughput & SLO clarifications

Thanks again for the productive call today — appreciate the time. I attached a short sample of our request traces (fastcart_workload_sample.csv) to help with sizing. A few clarifying points so your team can produce a realistic sizing: 

- Typical request profiles:
  • Non-streaming (batch-ish) requests: ~420 tokens/request average
  • Streaming sessions (real-time UI): incremental events ~160-220 tokens, typical session produces ~3 events on average
- Steady-state: ~25 QPS (business hours)
- Market-triggered peak: ~250 QPS sustained for short windows (1–3 minutes), occasionally cascades into 6–8 minute spikes
- Peak concurrency: ~220 concurrent streaming sessions during spikes
- Latency target (customer-facing): p95 generation time <= 600ms for short responses, and p95 <= 2s for longer generation flows. p50 should be <250ms ideally.
- Important: ~35% of our traffic is streaming events (real-time), rest is non-streaming API calls.

Two asks for the sizing: 
1) Please indicate tokens/sec and QPS assumptions you’re using for steady vs peak and the instance footprint we’d need for a reserved vs autoscaled approach.
2) Call out any SLO caveats for streaming sessions (tail latency during bursts) and recommendations for prefix/KV reuse.

We can share full traces if that helps — I can loop in our infra lead. Next week works for a follow-up.

Best,
Elena

Elena — thanks for the sample and the clear bullets. Quick recap + a couple of follow-ups so we size conservatively: 

Recap of what we see from your note: steady ~25 QPS, burst to ~250 QPS, ~35% streaming mix, avg tokens non-streaming ~420, streaming incremental ~160–220. Peak concurrency ~220 streaming sessions. Latency targets p95 <=600ms (short), <=2s (long).

Questions that will materially change the footprint:
- Can you confirm the average total tokens per streaming session (all events combined) and the average session duration in seconds?
- Are prefix/KV reuse opportunities realistic for you (i.e., are many requests re-using a short prompt prefix or are sessions mostly unique)?
- Do you need strict end-to-end tail SLO (99.9% p95) during bursts or is a tiered SLO acceptable (e.g., stricter during steady-state, softer during 5-minute burst windows)?

Proposed timeline: we’ll produce an initial sizing + estimate (constrained vs. cost-optimized) in 3 business days once we confirm the session-level tokens and whether you can provide 1 hour of traces for a recent spike.

Next owners: Marissa will lead the sizing/estimate, Dylan will propose an integration/test plan we can run in the pilot environment. I’ll coordinate logistics and the follow-up call.

On that note — @Marissa: can you draft two options (reserved baseline + autoscale + quantized variant) and include expected tokens/sec math and latency-risk notes?

Thanks,

Subject: FastCart preliminary sizing options (assumptions + estimates)

Hi Elena — based on the sample and Jonas’s notes I ran two quick sizing sketches (attached: fastcart_sizing_estimate_v1.xlsx). High-level assumptions I used: 

- Avg tokens/request (non-streaming): 420
- Avg tokens/event (streaming incremental): 180
- Steady-state: 25 QPS (mostly non-streaming)
- Peak: 250 QPS for 3 minutes (mix preserved)
- Streaming fraction: 35% of requests are streaming; we model streaming as long-lived connections with incremental generation per event

Derived tokens/sec and rough compute needs:
- Steady tokens/sec = (25 QPS * (0.65*420 + 0.35*180)) ≈ 8,850 tokens/sec
- Peak tokens/sec = (250 QPS * (0.65*420 + 0.35*180)) ≈ 88,500 tokens/sec
- Peak concurrent streams ~220 -> requires keeping ~220 KV caches hot; memory footprint and KV-serving will impact node count more than raw token throughput here

Option A — Reserved (conservative)
- Footprint: 4 x GPU nodes (A100-80GB-equivalent) with pinned model variant, pre-warmed KV caches
- Expected steady p95 generation: ~300–450ms; peak p95: 700ms–2s depending on cache hit rates
- Monthly estimate: $XXk–$YYk (see sheet)

Option B — Cost-optimized (autoscale + quantized model)
- Footprint: 2 x GPU baseline + autoscale policy to add capacity during detected peaks; run a 4-bit quantized variant for non-sensitive traffic
- Expected steady p95: ~350–600ms; peak p95: could degrade beyond 2s in worst-case burst unless autoscaling adds capacity fast enough and prefix caching hits are >60%
- Monthly estimate: ~$ZZk (see sheet)

Notes & SLO caveats:
- Streaming tail is sensitive to cache churn. If many unique sessions prevent cache reuse, latency will degrade quickly under burst. We recommend a short-lived pre-warm (keep-alive windows) for expected peak windows and a warming policy triggered by the first 10% of the predicted spike.
- If you need firm 99.9% p95 during the 3–8 minute peaks, reserved capacity (Option A) or a hybrid reserved+burst pool is the safer route.

Next: I’ll finalize numbers once Elena confirms session-level token totals and if you can share the 1-hour spike traces. I included a column in the sheet for sensitivity to cache hit rates.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we were hoping for. A few clarifications from our side after checking traces (see attached image client_traffic_spike_2027-10-29.png):

- Streaming sessions: average total tokens per session (all events) ~520 tokens; average session length ~24 seconds
- Non-streaming requests remain ~420 tokens average
- Peak windows: main spikes tend to last ~3 minutes but we saw a cascade up to ~8 minutes on Oct 29 — the attached image shows the cascade pattern
- Concurrency: at peak we observed ~220 concurrent streams; sustained concurrent non-streaming connections were ~60 concurrently executing requests in the 3-minute window

A couple product asks:
- What are the implications if we increase prefix reuse (we have some shared starting prompts) — will that reduce the node count materially?
- For pilot: can we run 1–2 one-hour stress tests that replicate the Oct 29 pattern? If so, what telemetry do you need from our side?

Also — we’re interested in a lower-latency premium tier for a subset of users (p95 <= 300ms). Is that something you can flag separately in the estimate?

Best,
Elena

Great context — very helpful. Summary of agreed items and owners (Mutual Action Plan attached):

1) Finalize sizing & pricing (Marissa) — deliverable: final XLS + two line items for: (a) Reserved baseline with pre-warm, (b) Hybrid autoscale + quantized variant + premium low-latency tier. Due: 2027-11-10
2) Pilot stress tests (Dylan) — schedule two 1-hour runs that reproduce Oct 29 cascade pattern. Redwood to provide test harness and required telemetry list (RTT, per-request tokens, model-level p50/p95/p99, cache-hit rates). Need traces from FastCart for exact request timing. Target window: week of 2027-11-15
3) Technical clarifications (Jonas) — confirm prefix reuse % and share 1 hour of spike traces. I’ll also send an example tracing template and a short pre-warm recommendation doc.

Preliminary answers to Elena’s asks: 
- Prefix reuse: if you can increase effective prefix reuse to >60% across streaming sessions, we typically see 30–45% reduction in required active memory footprint and a ~20–40% improvement in p95 during bursts (depends on model architecture).
- Premium tier: yes — we can surface a low-latency tier (p95<=300ms) by dedicating a hot micro-pool (smaller batch sizes, strict routing). I’ll include costing for that in Marissa’s estimate.

Attachments: redwood_mutual_action_plan.md (action list + dates).

Next call: propose Tue 2027-11-09 16:00 UTC to review sizing draft — Jonas to send invite.

Thanks all —
